content:
Snap has released the design of its consumer-grade Spectacles glasses this June, and now announces that the glasses are available for pre-order starting today, equipped with a brand new 5G portable carrying case. The company has also launched an active AI assistant named Specs Intelligence. Although named after Specs, both iPhone and Mac users can use it regardless of whether they own Specs glasses.

Mobile version of Specs launched in collaboration with Verizon

Snap today announced that it will launch a mobile network portable carrying case for Snap Specs, allowing users to use Specs when out and about. The carrying case can be purchased separately or added to the glasses for an additional US$200, bringing the total to US$2,395.

The mobile data plan for Specs will be US$10 per month for Verizon customers and US$20 for non-Verizon customers. Outside the United States, France's Orange and the UK's EE will also offer mobile data plans for Specs.

Specs is expected to begin shipping to customers later this fall, but an exact date has not been announced. In addition, Snap will open an experiential store on October 1 at the Westfield Century City in Los Angeles, allowing eagerly awaiting customers to try them on first. Verizon stores will also offer try-on services later.

Customers can pre-order Specs starting today with a refundable US$200 deposit here.

Specs Intelligence

Snap has also joined the race for personal AI assistants, launching a brand new Specs Intelligence app for iPhone and Mac. Although named after Specs, users do not need to own Specs glasses to use it — though the app works perfectly with Specs. Below is the company's description of this service:

It gradually learns about your goals, priorities, relationships and daily habits through the apps and tools you choose to connect, helping you focus on what's important in front of you while progressively advancing your long-term goals. SPECS Intelligence does not passively wait for instructions; it is designed to anticipate when assistance is needed and proactively provide relevant information and suggestions at the right moments. On SPECS AR glasses, it brings this personalised information into the real world, presented directly before your eyes.

The app is available on its website starting today, with a waitlist in place.
